blinding_guess.why: field:rcl_interfaces/GetParameters.values: _get_parameters_callback (parameter_service.py:79-88) replaces the whole response with an empty list (node.get_parameters([])) as soon as one requested name is undeclared or uninitialized, whereas the srv definition promises a list of the same length and order as the requested names with PARAMETER_NOT_SET entries for unset parameters; the snapshot's tests assert results.values == [] (test_parameter_service.py:76, test_parameter_client.py:199), so a caller indexing values by request position gets nothing.

notes: rclpy is the Python client library, so it contains no interface definitions and no application node: the parameter services are created by ParameterService for every Node at '<node name>/get_parameters' and '<node name>/list_parameters' (relative to the node namespace), and the node name 'param_demo' and the parameters 'param_1'/'param_2' would be supplied at run time by application code outside this package. I recorded the two service elements under declares because the type and name pattern are fixed in code; only the node-name prefix is runtime. The msg and field elements are defined in rcl_interfaces, not in this snapshot, so they are in not_declared and, because the code imports and populates them, also in references. No ports were recorded for param:param_1/param:param_2 because this package does not declare or serve them by name. QoS: the code fixes qos_profile_parameters for all parameter services; its concrete values come from rmw_qos_profile_parameters in rmw (outside the snapshot), and I recorded reliability/durability from the snapshot's own documentation comments in qos.py; deadline is not set (null). QoS for the msg/field ports is null because they are not endpoints. The manifest version 7.0.1 does not match the Iron rclpy series as far as I know, but per instructions dependency definitions were fetched at the rcl_interfaces Iron release tag 1.6.0. To identify that tag I also requested the same two .srv files at 1.6.1 and 1.6.2 (404), and at 1.7.0 and the iron branch (byte-identical to 1.6.0); only 1.6.0 was used for hashing. definition_id values are the sha256_normalised proxy, not ROS 2 type hashes. rclpy's parameter_client.py also calls '<remote node>/get_parameters' and '<remote node>/list_parameters' with names supplied at run time; those consumed uses are not listed in references.
